title: Isandro and the Gravity
premise: Theo Underhill navigates the Meridian Loop, a freight run between two colonies that severed contact decades ago, carrying cryopods from both worlds whose passengers were never claimed. When a manifest update lists a passenger — Isandro Vey — aboard the Halcyon, a ship destroyed before it ever launched, Theo discovers the pods hold two halves of one divided humanity, and someone is quietly deciding who wakes. Pursued by the Concord's enforcers and guided by Isandro's ghost-coded messages, Theo must choose which half of humanity wakes first: their own world, or the enemy they've never met. In the end, Theo refuses the binary, waking both halves together in the neutral dark of deep space and forging a fragile found family from the ship's scattered crew.
about_author: Noor Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent six years relaying messages between ships that rarely spoke to each other directly. They write science fiction about people who keep systems running long after anyone remembers why.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Establishes the Meridian Loop, the silent colonies of Ceres Verge and Ashfall, and the 4,000 unclaimed cryopods in the hold that Theo talks to on night shifts. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as routine; Theo knows every pod by name and none by face.

chapters.title: A Name That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A routine manifest sync lists ISANDRO VEY aboard the Halcyon — a ship that burned on its cradle before launch, twenty years ago. The manifest is signed with Theo's own authorization code, which they never used. Emotional beat: dread blooming inside familiarity.

chapters.title: Passenger Manifest
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Juno Reyes, the ship's skeptical engineer. They trace the entry to a hidden partition in the cargo AI, where Isandro's voice logs wait like letters. He claims to be a pod technician from Ashfall who discovered the wake-lists are rigged. Emotional beat: cautious wonder; grief finding a shape.

chapters.title: Two Halves of One Hold
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Inventory reveals the truth: half the pods are Ceres Verge citizens, half Ashfall, and the Concord's wake protocol will only revive one registry. The crew votes on whether to report it. Emotional beat: the first fracture — duty versus conscience.

chapters.title: What the Concord Keeps
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A Concord inspection vessel docks, led by Auditor Sefa Idris, who seems to already know about Isandro. She offers Theo promotion and silence. Theo finds evidence the 'war' that severed the colonies was staged to justify the split manifests. Emotional beat: betrayal; the law revealed as a machine for forgetting.

chapters.title: Ghost Code
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV (via recovered logs). His life unfolds: a pod tech who smuggled proof of the rigged lists into the AI before the Halcyon fire, knowing he wouldn't survive. He addresses Theo directly — he chose them, a navigator who still talks to sleepers. Emotional beat: intimacy across death; being seen.

chapters.title: Running the Dark
chapters.summary: Full-crew POV rotation. The Concord orders the Meridian scuttled with all pods jettisoned as 'hazardous cargo.' The crew burns their route credentials and takes the ship off-grid into an unmapped dust shoal. Emotional beat: terror becoming commitment; strangers becoming crew.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Waking
chapters.summary: Juno and Theo's POV. Power calculations show they can wake only half the pods before life support fails — the choice Isandro died trying to expose. The crew splits bitterly along colony lines. Theo realizes any choice repeats the crime. Emotional beat: despair at the math of mercy.

chapters.title: Isandro and the Gravity
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, climax. Cornered by Idris in the dust shoal, Theo broadcasts Isandro's logs fleet-wide and offers the third option: wake everyone slowly, all halves together, drifting as one settlement in the dark while the colonies watch. Idris's own crew defects when they hear the names read aloud. Emotional beat: defiance as love; gravity as the pull toward each other.

chapters.title: Everyone Wakes Somewhere
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Months later: the first revivals, Ceres Verge and Ashfall faces meeting in the same corridor, clumsy and human. The Meridian becomes a slow ark; Theo finally stops talking to the pods because the people answer back. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not granted; justice outside the law, kept alive by ordinary hands.
